papers.what_it_is: A review of tensor-network applications in quantum computing: simulation, circuit synthesis, error correction and mitigation, and quantum machine learning.

assertions.value: The authors state that the paper reviews tensor-network applications in quantum computing across simulation of quantum computation, quantum circuit synthesis, quantum error correction and mitigation, and quantum machine learning.
quotes: quantum circuit synthesis, quantum error correction and mitigation, and quantum machine learning
assertions.certainty_reason: The introduction states the review's scope.

assertions.value: The authors cite the Eckart-Young theorem as stating that, for approximations with a fixed rank, the solution provided by SVD is optimal.
quotes: the Eckart–Young theorem [9] states that for approximations with a fixed rank, the solution provided by SVD is optimal.
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that the contraction cost of the matrix product state is polynomial in the system size, so physical observables can be evaluated efficiently.
quotes: Its contraction cost is polynomial in the system size, meaning the physical observables can be evaluated efficiently.
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that algorithms for projected entangled pair states are typically much more computationally demanding than those for matrix product states.
quotes: algorithms for PEPS are typically much more computationally demanding
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that the multiscale entanglement renormalization ansatz can reproduce a logarithmic violation of the area law.
quotes: can reproduce logarithmic violation of the area law.
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that the optimal contraction cost of the pairwise-contraction approach still generally scales exponentially.
quotes: The optimal contraction cost of this approach still generally scales exponentially [18]
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that approximate contraction is not expected to be viable in the general case, while evidence from many-body physics systems shows that many real world tensor networks are tractable approximately.
quotes: While even this is not expected to be viable in the general case [73]
many real world tensor networks are tractable approximately
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that an efficient classical algorithm for estimating the probability of a given output of random circuit sampling would lead to the collapse of the polynomial hierarchy, citing two works.
quotes: the existence of an efficient classical algorithm for estimating the probability of a given output would lead to the collapse of the polynomial hierarchy [96, 97]
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that many tensor-network methods were later shown to solve the kicked Ising problem more efficiently, and to produce more accurate results than the quantum processor itself.
quotes: can solve the same problem more efficiently, and can even produce more accurate results than the quantum processor itself.
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that earlier random circuit sampling experiments can now be simulated, while the more recent experiments with better fidelity and larger circuit volume remain hard.
quotes: the more recent experiments with better fidelity and larger circuit volume still remain hard
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors report that one cited study claimed approximate classical MPS and PEPS methods cannot match the quantum simulator's solution quality, that a later belief-propagation simulation achieved comparable accuracy for two- and three-dimensional systems, and that no such simulation was done for the biclique lattice.
quotes: approximate classical TN methods such as MPS and PEPS cannot match the solution quality of the quantum simulator
no such simulation was performed for the infinite dimensional biclique lattice
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper presents a contested result and does not resolve it.

assertions.value: The authors report that the largest boson sampling experiments were simulated on up to 288 GPUs in under two hours, and conclude that no boson sampling experiments demonstrate clear evidence for beyond classical hardness.
quotes: up to 288 GPUs in under two hours [7]
no boson sampling experiments demonstrate clear evidence for beyond classical hardness
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that promoting a tensor network to quantum gates takes four steps: transform to isometric tensors, embed spatial and temporal directions, promote each isometry to a unitary, and decompose each unitary into gates.
quotes: (i) transforming the original TN into a TN of isometric tensors; (ii) embedding spatial and temporal directions to the network; (iii) promoting each isometric tensor into a unitary; and (iv) decomposing each unitary as quantum gates.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section IV.A defines the procedure.

assertions.value: The authors state that an MPS can be exactly transformed into a canonical form with only isometric tensors.
quotes: an MPS can be exactly transformed into a canonical form, including only isometric tensors
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that a PEPS cannot be exactly mapped onto a quantum circuit without an exponential amount of postselection.
quotes: one cannot exactly map a PEPS onto a quantum circuit without an exponential amount of postselection
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that exact MPS preparation requires unitary operations acting on (⌊log(m)⌋ + 1) qubits, where m is an MPS bond dimension, and note this may be undesirable on hardware with limited connectivity.
quotes: (⌊log(m)⌋ + 1) qubits, where m is an MPS bond dimension
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that the MERA features intrinsic robustness to noise and does not suffer from barren plateaus.
quotes: It features an intrinsic robustness to noise and does not suffer from barren plateaus [152–154].
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that adaptive circuits can prepare certain states in constant depth, whereas pure unitary circuits need a depth scaling with system size for long-range correlated states.
quotes: adaptive circuits can prepare certain states in constant-depth.
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that convolutional codes, concatenated block codes and topological codes can respectively be represented by the MPS, tree tensor networks and PEPS.
quotes: can be respectively represented by the MPS, tree TNs, and PEPS.
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that any qudit QEC code can be represented by a tensor network built out of three elementary seed tensors.
quotes: any qudit QEC code can be represented by a TN built out
of three elementary seed tensors [176]
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that tensor-network codes come with optimal decoders evaluated by contracting a tensor network.
quotes: TN codes come naturally equipped with optimal decoders that are evaluated by contracting a TN
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that tensor-network decoders are considered highly accurate but not practical for real time decoding.
quotes: TN decoders are, up to date, considered as highly accurate but not practical for real time decoding [210].
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that the sample overhead of probabilistic error cancellation grows exponentially with the number of qubits and circuit depths.
quotes: growing exponentially with the number of qubits and circuit depths.
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that tensor-network error mitigation provides a universal lower cost bound for error mitigation, specifically a quadratic cost reduction.
quotes: TEM provides a universal lower cost bound for error mitigation, specifically a quadratic cost reduction.
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that tensor-network error mitigation was experimentally demonstrated on a circuit of 91 qubits with 4095 two-qubit gates.
quotes: it was experimentally demonstrated on a 91-qubit circuit with 4095 two-qubit gates.
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state it is an open question whether error mitigation alone, or combined with quantum error correction, can lead to utility in near-term quantum computation.
quotes: an open question whether error mitigation alone, or in combination with quantum error correction, can lead to utility
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the open question in Section V.C.

assertions.value: The authors state that in regression and classification TN-QML obtains a TN layer's output by measuring observables on the quantum state rather than performing costly tensor contractions on classical hardware.
quotes: TN-QML obtains the output of a TN neural layer by measuring observables on the corresponding quantum state rather than performing costly tensor contractions on classical hardware.
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in quantum simulation, parameterizing tensor networks with quantum gates has been shown to offer an exponential reduction in the number of parameters needed to match classical tensor networks, which could potentially translate to machine learning tasks.
quotes: has been shown to offer an exponential reduction in the number of parameters required to achieve results similar to those of classical TNs [146, 149]
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that variational TN circuits offer an advantage over hardware-efficient ansatze in being free from barren plateaus.
quotes: being free from barren plateaus
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that recent work argues the quantum convolutional neural network, once considered a candidate for exponential quantum advantage, can be dequantized using classical shadow techniques.
quotes: recent work [239] has argued against this, suggesting it can be dequantized using classical shadow techniques.
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that it remains to be seen whether TN-QML can offer any polynomial advantage.
quotes: it remains to be seen whether TN-QML can offer any polynomial advantage in this context.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section VII states the open question.

assertions.value: The authors state that finding a polynomial-time tensor-network algorithm for a problem proves the problem is in the complexity class P.
quotes: finding a polynomial-time tensor-network algorithm for a problem [246] proves that the problem is in the complexity class P.
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.
assertions.reader_inference: The statement is true only if the algorithm is exact and provably polynomial for all inputs; the paper does not say so.

assertions.value: The authors state that highly accurate TN decoding is too slow for real-time hardware decoding, and suggest designing heuristic algorithms that approximate it.
quotes: too slow for real-time hardware decoding [210]
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that in holographic preparation of a TN state, once a circuit finishes preparing one site the qubit can be reused for the next site.
quotes: once a circuit is done preparing one site, the qubit can be reused to prepare the next site.
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that slicing splits a contraction into many smaller independent contractions, addressing the space cost of intermediate memory.
quotes: Slicing (also known as cutting or projecting) splits a contraction into many smaller independent contractions
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited or author-stated; not proved here.
